illustrations.title: Noah's Ark
illustrations.alt: Cutaway drawing of Noah's ark with three decks, a door in the side and a ramp, with side, front, top and cross-section views and the dimensions 300 by 50 by 30 cubits
illustrations.caption: The ark as Genesis 6:14–16 describes it: 300 cubits long, 50 wide and 30 high (about 137 × 23 × 14 m), with lower, middle and upper decks, a door in its side and an opening for light a cubit below the roof. The proportions are the text's; the shape and the details are one reconstruction.

illustrations.title: Jericho
illustrations.alt: Artist's impression of walled Jericho: a ditch, an outer and an inner wall with houses between them, a gate with two towers, a citadel, with a cross-section through the walls and a detail of the main gate
illustrations.caption: An artist's impression of Jericho (Tell es-Sultan), by the spring that still waters the oasis and one of the oldest walled towns known. Its Bronze Age defences were a stone retaining wall at the foot of the mound with a mudbrick wall on it, and a second wall higher up; on the north side excavators found houses built against the lower wall, which recalls Rahab's house “built into the wall” (2:15). The last walled city ended in fallen mudbrick and a fire that left storage jars still full of grain (compare 6:20, 24). Its date is debated: Garstang, and later Bryant Wood, put it about 1400 BC; Kathleen Kenyon about 1550 BC. The drawing simplifies the city's plan.
